newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips end down, 2nd board rebounds.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips end down, 2nd board rebounds.

text.p: Falls in Malaysian heavyweight blue-chip shares dragged the key market index lower at the close, but secondary stocks rebounded on renewed buying in the last hour, dealers said.

"The second board came alive an hour before the close though buying was not very aggresive," said a S.J. Securities dealer. "Overall, the market was pretty quiet today with institutions absent after yesterday's spate of buying."
The Composite Index ended down 5.69 points at 1,183.52. The Second Board index closed at 648.65, up 3.76 points, after hitting an intra-day low of 643.80.
Leading the drop among blue chips were Tenaga Nasional, Genting and Proton, all down 20 cents.

Dealers and analysts said local institutional support for power utility Tenaga appeared to be over. "At 11 ringgit, Tenaga is near an 18-month high," said Audrey Ho, head of research at Mohaiyani Securities.

Analysts said they expect the market to extend its consolidation after the recent run-up. "It will not be so soon before we can see another round of buying. The market looks a bit tired," said an analyst with a foreign securities house.
